definitions.gloss: block script, regular script, standard script
definitions.explanation: A style of writing Chinese characters (kanji) in which each stroke is clearly and separately formed, without cursive connections. The most standard and legible of the traditional calligraphy styles.

examples.japanese: {楷書|かいしょ}で{丁寧|ていねい}に{書|か}いてください。
examples.english: Please write carefully in block script.

examples.japanese: {書道|しょどう}では{楷書|かいしょ}から{練習|れんしゅう}を{始|はじ}める。
examples.english: In calligraphy, practice begins with block script.

examples.japanese: {公的|こうてき}な{書類|しょるい}には{楷書|かいしょ}で{記入|きにゅう}するよう{求|もと}められることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Official documents often require entries to be written in block script.

notes:
USAGE:
One of the five traditional styles of Chinese calligraphy. {楷書|かいしょ} is the most standard and readable style, making it the default for formal documents and the starting point for calligraphy students. When filling out official forms in Japan, instructions often specify {楷書|かいしょ}で (in block script).

RELATED SCRIPTS:
- {行書|ぎょうしょ}: semi-cursive script (partially connected strokes)
- {草書|そうしょ}: cursive script (highly abbreviated, flowing)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {楷書|かいしょ}で{書|か}く: to write in block script
- {楷書|かいしょ}{体|たい}: block script style
- {楷書|かいしょ}で{記入|きにゅう}する: to fill in using block script
